• Education: No strict formal entry requirements, though a Grade 3 (or equivalent) in GCSE Maths and English is desirable.
• Skills & Attributes: Strong communication, reliability, excellent work ethic, a can-do attitude, and the ability to follow technical instructions and work well independently or in a team.
• No prior experience required—full on-the-job training will be provided.
BOOST YOUR APPLICATION

What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? Is it our aircraft, innovation, global impact, or something else? Let us know what interests you about our work and why we stand out to you.

Why do you want to learn by doing? We’d love to hear what draws you to practical, skills-based learning.

• DIY projects
• Building and fixing things
• Doing make-up or beauty work
• Tinkering and Tech Projects
• Building models
• Baking or cooking

We love seeing what you are passionate about. If you've worked on any hands-on projects—whether it's building, baking, fixing something —we'd be thrilled to see it!
Feel free to attach photos, documents, or a short video showcasing a project you're proud of. This isn't a requirement, but it’s a fantastic way to give us a glimpse of your practical skills. We can't wait to see your work!

The Role
We are seeking a full-time Power Market Analyst to join Wood Mackenzie’s Power & Renewables team, focusing on the development and application of advanced power market models across European electricity markets.
As a Power Market Analyst, you will play a key role in building, maintaining, and enhancing market optimization models used to analyse power systems, generation economics, transmission constraints, and market outcomes. You will apply linear programming (LP) and other optimization techniques to simulate market behaviour, assess investment and operational decisions, and provide actionable insights on power market dynamics, decarbonization pathways, and energy transition challenges.
Key Responsibilities
• Develop, maintain, and enhance optimization-based power market models for European electricity markets.
• Design and implement LP and mixed-integer optimization models to simulate generation dispatch, storage operation, cross-border trading, and market-clearing mechanisms.
• Analyse power market fundamentals, including supply-demand dynamics, renewable integration, fuel markets, emissions costs, and transmission constraints.
• Conduct scenario analysis to evaluate market outcomes, asset profitability, policy impacts, and energy transition pathways.
• Translate complex model outputs into clear market insights and recommendations for internal stakeholders and clients.
• Improve model methodologies, assumptions, and analytical frameworks to enhance model accuracy, transparency, and performance.
• Work with large datasets and develop efficient data workflows to support model development and analysis.
• Collaborate with experts across power markets, renewable energy, economics, and policy to deliver high-quality research and market intelligence.
• Monitor developments in European energy markets, regulatory frameworks, and market design, assessing their impact on market participants and investment decisions.
• Support client engagements through presentations, bespoke analyses, technical discussions, and thought leadership.
About You
We are looking for a highly analytical and intellectually curious individual with a strong foundation in optimization, quantitative modelling, and power market analysis. You enjoy solving complex problems, building robust models, and generating insights that support strategic decision-making.
Essential Skills and Qualifications
• A degree in Operations Research, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Economics, Energy Systems, Computer Science, or a related quantitative discipline.
• Experience in electricity market analysis, power system modeling, or energy economics.
• Strong knowledge of optimization techniques, particularly linear programming (LP) and mixed-integer programming (MIP).
• Experience developing and implementing mathematical models for power systems, generation portfolios, storage assets, or electricity markets.
• Proficiency in Python and/or other programming languages used for optimization and quantitative analysis.
• Experience with optimization frameworks and solvers such as Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, Pyomo, or similar tools.
• Strong understanding of European power market fundamentals, market design, and price formation mechanisms.
• Ability to analyze complex datasets and communicate technical findings clearly to both technical and commercial audiences.
• Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.
Why Join Us?
At Wood Mackenzie, you will work on industry-leading power market models that help clients navigate rapidly changing energy markets and the transition to a low-carbon economy. You will collaborate with leading analysts, modelers, and industry experts to solve complex challenges facing power systems, renewable integration, energy storage, and electricity market design.
This role offers an opportunity to apply cutting-edge optimization techniques and market analysis to inform investment decisions, support policy evaluation, and shape the future of the energy sector.

We tackle the most complex problems in quantitative finance, by bringing scientific clarity to financial complexity.
From our London HQ, we unite world-class researchers and engineers in an environment that values deep exploration and methodical execution, because the best ideas take time to evolve. Together we're building a world-class platform to amplify our teams' most powerful ideas.
As part of our engineering team, you'll shape the platforms and tools that drive high-impact research, designing systems that scale, accelerate discovery and support innovation across the firm.
Take the next step in your career.
The role
G-Research is investing in how we apply large language models (LLMs) and other Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques across the firm. We are looking for an exceptional NLP Performance Engineer to join our NLP Engineering team and take ownership of large-scale LLM inference performance.
This is a specialist Quantitative Developer role. Like all our Quantitative Developers, you will work alongside researchers to bring their ideas to life, with a particular focus on maximising the performance of LLMs.
This is a hands-on, high-impact role. You will design and implement techniques that improve the performance, cost-efficiency and capabilities of inference workloads on cutting-edge compute infrastructure, enabling researchers and engineers to make the best use of current and future systems.
Working closely with research teams and infrastructure engineers, you will profile and analyse workloads, eliminate bottlenecks and develop reference solutions. Your work will help shape the tooling and infrastructure that underpins our NLP capabilities.
Key responsibilities of the role include:
• Profiling, benchmarking and optimising large-scale LLM inference workloads across our compute infrastructure
• Ensuring efficient deployment of the latest models across a range of GPU architectures, adapting the inference stack as hardware evolves
• Designing and implementing inference optimisations while maintaining output quality
• Developing reference implementations, libraries and tooling to improve the efficiency and reliability of NLP workloads
• Collaborating with researchers, senior stakeholders and engineers to design optimised solutions
• Working with systems, architecture and platform teams to evolve the compute stack and influence long-term platform decisions
Who are we looking for?
We're looking for an engineer who combines deep knowledge of LLM inference with strong software engineering skills and a scientific approach to performance.
The ideal candidate will have the following skills and experience:
• A Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD in computer science, or equivalent experience
• Proven experience profiling, benchmarking and optimising large-scale LLM inference workloads
• A scientific, evidence-led approach to performance optimisation, using rigorous benchmarking and reproducible measurement
• Deep understanding of transformer inference, including prefill versus decode, KV-cache behaviour, attention variants and performance bottlenecks
• Hands-on experience with LLM serving frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or TGI, and the PyTorch ecosystem
• Experience with inference optimisation techniques, including quantisation, speculative decoding and model parallelism across modern GPU architectures
• Strong software engineering skills, including Python, CUDA and building reliable systems for machine learning workloads
• Strong communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across research, infrastructure and engineering teams
Why join us?
• Highly competitive compensation plus annual discretionary bonus

• Informal dress code and excellent work/life balance

Fixed Term, full-time (minimum 6 months)

Application Deadline: 15th October 2026
About Springer Nature
Springer Nature is one of the leading publishers of research in the world. We publish the largest number of journals and books and are a pioneer in open research. Through our leading brands, trusted for more than 180 years, we provide technology-enabled products, platforms and services that help researchers to uncover new ideas and share their discoveries, health professionals to stay at the forefront of medical science, and educators to advance learning. We are proud to be part of progress, working together with the communities we serve to share knowledge and bring greater understanding to the world. For more information, please visit about.springernature.com and follow @SpringerNature.
At Springer Nature, we recognise that great talent develops through many different paths. We encourage applications from individuals with strong transferable skills, provided they are supported by relevant experience that shows how those skills have been successfully applied in practice. Our hiring approach balances skills, experience, and potential to ensure each role is fulfilled with both short-term effectiveness and long-term growth in mind.
About the Brand
Nature Portfolio’s high-quality journals and services across the life, physical, chemical and applied sciences help move science and society forward.
Nature Portfolio is home to the leading, international weekly journal of science, Nature – founded in 1869. It is also home to the Nature research and Nature Reviews journals, the leading open access multidisciplinary journal Nature Communications, and open access journals including Scientific Reports. Together, these journals publish some of the world's most significant scientific discoveries.
About the Role
Do you love science but feel that a career at the bench isn’t enough to sate your desire to learn more about scientific research? Do you enjoy reading papers outside your chosen area of research? If the answer is ‘yes’ to any or all these questions, you could be the person we’re looking for to join the Nature Portfolio editorial team. To help us build on the success of the portfolio, we’re seeking an editor with experience in geophysics who has a critical eye, a deep understanding of their subject and interests beyond, and who can think on their feet.​ Knowledge of seismology, tectonics, geodynamics, and natural hazards would be desirable as would interests in glaciology and geomorphology.
Nature Geoscience is a monthly online and print journal that publishes the very best research from across the Earth and planetary sciences. The aim of this highly selective title is to understand Earth's history and its future evolution through publication of primary research, synthesis, news and opinion-type articles from across the broad spectrum of geosciences, encompassing field work, modelling and theoretical studies.
The location(s) strategy supports team structure and aligns business needs.

• Scientific Comprehension - Contributing to content and strategy in this area at Nature Geoscience
• Scientific & Academic Writing - Commissioning, editing content such as Reviews, or writing editorials.

Essential
• A PhD (or equivalent) in a field related to geophysics.

• A passion for science and a thirst to learn more. You must be able to demonstrate the breadth of your interest in scientific research, both within and beyond your specialty.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including fluent English (written and spoken).
• The ability to read and assess the novelty, context and implications of research submitted to the journal from different areas of this discipline.
• Be eager to travel and meet scientists worldwide, learn more about them and their research, and help them learn more about us and what we are looking for in the papers we seek to publish.
Desirable
• Additional research experience valuable but not needed.
• Editorial experience is not required, although applicants with editorial experience are encouraged to apply and may be considered for Senior Editor positions.
The successful candidates will report to the Chief Editor of the journal.
This demanding and intellectually stimulating role is offered in London/Milano/Pune but we are open to applications from internal candidates from other editorial offices.
Applications must include:
• A brief cover letter (one page) explaining your interest in the role, relevant experience, preferred office location, salary expectations, and current notice period.
• A CV detailing your relevant skills and experience, employment history, education, and any achievements demonstrating your suitability for the position.
• A concise discussion (maximum 500 words) of a 2026 research article that was not published in Nature Geoscience. The article should excite you and reflect topics relevant to the advertised role. Your discussion should include:
• A brief summary of the article and its main findings
• Relevant context from the broader scientific literature
• Discussion of whether this article could have been a good fit for publication in Nature Geoscience, taking into consideration the aims and scope of the journal.

Big responsibility. Personal support. That’s Beyond the Ordinary.

The programme starts on Monday, 20th September 2027, for an organisation-wide induction (you need to be able to attend).
A bit about Audit
Audit at BDO gives you the chance to take on meaningful work early in your career. We’re the only UK mid-market organisation with more than £1bn in turnover and 8,000 people. That means you get the scale and breadth of a major professional services business, while working with clients where your contribution can make a real difference.

Over three years, you’ll build hands-on experience while working towards a recognised professional qualification, the ACA.

You’ll have support around you as you take those next steps and build towards where you want your career to go.

As for you
You’re curious, resilient and adaptable. You’re ready to learn, ask questions and take on more responsibility as you grow.
Bring your problem-solving, analytical skills and critical thinking. We’ll give you opportunities to put them into practice, alongside the support to keep developing.
Join us in one of our hubs in Guildford, Gatwick, Reading or Southampton.

• A minimum 2:2 degree in any discipline (obtained or predicted)

• GCSEs at grade 4 and above in Maths and English, or Scottish National 5 grade A-C. You’ll also need to provide evidence if successful
• Commitment to balance study and professional work
• The right to work in the UK (we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for these roles as they do not meet the current minimum salary requirements for sponsorship set by the Home Office. Applications from candidates who have their own legal right to work within the UK must cover the duration of their 3-year training contract and employment)
How the interview process will go
We want you to know what to expect, so here’s the typical process:
• Online application form.
• Online assessments.
• Video interview.
• Virtual assessment centre.
• Final interview in person.
We’ll keep you updated at each stage and share tips to help you prepare. And just so you know: we don’t use AI in any part of our candidate screening process. Every application is reviewed by a real person.
What you get in return
Our benefits are designed to support your life in and outside of work, with options including additional leave, gym membership and employee discounts, alongside pension, health and wellbeing support and a range of protection benefits.
Salary
£30,000 - £32,000 dependable on location.
Closing date for applications is Sunday 15th November 2026.
Before you go
Wherever you join BDO, you’ll have the chance to learn by doing, work with clients and build your career with people around you to support your development.
The opportunity to build your experience, confidence and career without having to do it alone.
Big responsibility. Personal support.
That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Apply now.

• Lead cross-disciplinary collaboration and coordination to ensure coherent system design across multiple subsystems and stakeholder groups

• Support integration & test of specified functionality and contribute to defect resolution.
Dependent on experience, you may also:
• Provide technical direction for the design, as well as promotion of good-practice and general guidance to the wider Systems team.
• Take responsibility for project deliverables or large scale work packages.
• Mentor, coach and potentially line-manage other engineers within the team.
What you’ll bring
Required Experience:
• Understanding of full-lifecycle Systems Engineering principles
• Experience in the design and capture of complex hardware, firmware and/or software interactions
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively to solve complex engineering challenges where design complexity and uncertainty is present
• Ability to work within an experienced multidisciplinary engineering team
• Experience in writing and managing technical requirements
Desirable Experience:
• Experience, or a strong interest in, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) including:
• Working in accordance with a defined architectural framework (preferably MagicGrid)
• Use of the Systems Modelling Language (SysML)
• Experience of defining and managing requirements, maintaining traceability through System and Subsystem design activities using IBM DOORS
• Awareness of RMT engineering principles such as (built-in-test, fault identification and isolation, failure handling/fault tolerance)
• Experience in integration, test, and verification of complex engineering products
• A desire to evaluate and improve processes and tools
• Experience of working in an agile lifecycle
• Experience of working with configuration management tools
• Experience using the Atlassian tool sets (Confluence, Jira and Bitbucket)
For those with extensive experience, we would also be looking for:
• Demonstrable experience within, and the ability to contribute to shape complex areas of system design
• Demonstrable experience taking responsibility for outcomes and contributing to technical decisions

Vehicle Shift Fitter
Would you love to be part of a professional engineering team that maintains and repairs a modern and varied fleet of vehicles?
How about developing your own technical skills on varied Public Service Vehicles? If that sounds like something you want to be involved in, we’d love to have you on board – and we’ll give you all the training and development you need to get to where you want to go!
Stagecoach Cumbria & North Lancashire operates 303 vehicles over 5 sites and our Carlisle team are looking for people from a background in vehicle mechanical / electrical engineering to be part of our growing team. You may be in a truck / HGV, rail, light commercial or automotive setting at the moment, but fancy a change of vehicle to enhance your skill-set.
Likewise, if you’ve got PCV experience, you’ll still find new opportunities to learn given the variety of our fleet.
Our Carlisle depot operates a varied range of vehicles from minibuses and Double Deckers on a daily basis ,we operate Alexander Dennis, Volvo and Optare vehicles.
You’ve probably seen some of our vehicles driving around Carlisle and surrounding area, transporting our fantastic customers across the Cumbria & other parts of the Country.
Those customers rely on our services to get them to work, to the high street, to hospitals, to days away and nights out – and as part of our engineering team you’ll be a key part in making sure our vehicles are in tip top condition to do just that. It’s a really important role within our depot, so we’ll make sure you’re as looked after as our vehicles are!
Don’t worry if you’ve not worked on these vehicles before (or indeed buses) – we’ll train you on everything you need to know, and you’ll be supported by a great team of fellow Electricians, Mechanics, Technicians and Engineering Managers who all pull together to do a brilliant job.
And interestingly it’s not all depot-based work – you could well find yourself out and about dealing with vehicle issues on the road, so it won’t always be the same four walls you’re looking at!
Aside from the reward of helping to deliver an incredible experience to our customers, there’s plenty more we can offer:
Job Security – we’ve been going since 1980, we turn over £1.3bn and we’re not planning on hanging our boots up anytime soon!
Safe Environment – we provide boots, overalls and specialist equipment so no need to worry about being safe and protected, or having the right kit for the job.
Free Travel – for you and your companion on our buses. That means on your days off you can be off shopping for free without worrying about parking the car, or heading off for a day in the city or the Lakes without paying a fortune in petrol or train fares!
Promotions – if you’re happy sticking as a Technician / Mechanic / Electrician then that’s absolutely fine by us…but if you do want to progress we’ll support you every step of the way. You will be given exposure to work which will develop your skills and experience to allow you to progress your career further. The vast majority of our Engineering Managers and Directors are home grown talent – so that could very well be you in the not too distant future!
So, if you have an engineering background with a vehicular slant (truck, haulage, automotive, plant, rail, farm – if it moves, it’s good experience for working on buses) and have a passion for great work with a great team, then we can’t wait to receive your application!

Job Title:
Electronics Design Engineer - Test Systems
Reporting To:
Manager, Test Systems Design
Work Schedule:

Moog Wolverhampton are currently recruiting for a Electronics Design Engineer - Test Systems at our facility in Wolverhampton.  The Electronics Design Engineer will be responsible for the development of application specific electronic and electrical solutions, from concept to detailed design, for integration into complex Test Equipment Systems. These Test Systems support the Qualification and Production Acceptance testing of a wide range of Moog Aircraft Flight Control Systems and Components.
The Electronic/ Electrical Design Engineer will support the role of Technical Review in the provision of Test Equipment Electronic/ Electrical Solutions within Moog Aircraft Group.
You will play a key role in maintaining strong relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders, supporting efficient financial operations across multiple UK sites.
Key Responsibilities
• Design analogue and digital electronic solutions to support the production and control of a wide range of hydro-mechanical & electro-mechanical Test Systems
• Application of safety and industry standards and guidelines in the design and integration of electronic and electrical solutions into Test Equipment Systems.
• Application of: top-level architecture, requirements definition, concept, design, verification & validation methods and final release for Test Systems.
• Assist the Test Systems Design Manager with the definition of electronic/ electrical solutions in the creation of detailed Test Equipment Proposals.
• Prepare and release documentation in support of the Test Equipment Common Development Process, including active participation at technical reviews with peers and Chief Engineers.
• Support Root Cause investigations into all aspects of the Test Equipment System and/ or components as required.
• Identify appropriate training courses to maintain electronic / electrical capabilities within Moog Wolverhampton Test Equipment Group
• Ensure all Health & Safety practices are followed and, any new issues raised during any work activities. Write or assist with the completion and review of work related Risk Assessments.
What You’ll Bring
• Bachelor Degree, preferably a Masters, in a relevant Electronic/ Electrical subject area as a minimum.
• Demonstrable commercial experience of complex analogue and digital electronics design. Particularly with application to closed loop control and transducer conditioning.
• Experience of the design and manufacture of industrial machines
• Minimum of 3 years’ experience in the development of Electronic/ electrical solutions for multi-axis, closed loop, servo-hydraulic and electromechanical Test Systems. Including the design, selection and application of Safety Related Equipment, PLCs and Motor Drive systems.
• Additional recognised qualifications in the application of Safety related Directives and Standards would be advantageous.
• Proficient in the use of diagnostic equipment to fault find electronic and electrical issues from first principles.
• Experience in one or more of the following: eCAD, PCB Software, LabView, DOORS, JIRA, MatLab and SubVersion is advantageous.
• Proficient in the use of Microsoft applications including Excel, Word, VISO and Project.
• Knowledge of PC operating platforms (DOS/ Windows/ Microsoft Environments) and Low Level Programming (C++, Visual Basic)

As part of a major electromechanical installation project at the Hinkley Point C nuclear construction site, the Site Facility Manager is responsible for defining, planning, implementing, operating, and maintaining all temporary facilities located outside the Turbine Hall, including offices, prefabrication workshops, storage areas, and related utilities.
The position reports to the Site Administrative & Finance Manager and works closely with the Technical Services and Procurement teams.
The Facility Manager is responsible for applying company policies regarding Safety, Quality, and Cost control.
Key Responsibilities and Activities
1. Planning, Mobilization, and Setup of Temporary Infrastructure
•
On-site mobilization planning: Define and organize—with support from the Site Manager, the Administrative & Financial Manager, and the Home Office—all steps required to open the site (preliminary studies, site layout planning, and identification of technical and logistical needs).
•
Needs assessment & Sizing: Evaluate and plan requirements regarding floor space, capacity, and technical constraints for project management offices, prefabrication workshops, and storage areas.
•
Layout coordination with assembly subcontractors: Manage and coordinate the physical layout of offices and prefabrication areas within the designated site footprint, working closely with assembly subcontractors to ensure smooth logistics and avoid operational conflicts.
•
Temporary infrastructure setup: Actively oversee the installation of site facilities (offices, auxiliary changing rooms, sanitary facilities, etc.), storage areas, access roads, fencing, and safety equipment on the land provided by the client.
•
Temporary utility coordination: Manage the installation and connection of essential site utilities (IT/Internet, electricity, water, telecommunications, and wastewater disposal).
•
Utility connection management: Independently manage the end-to-end distribution and compliance of utility networks, extending from the connection points (tapping points) provided by the client to our offices, storage areas, and prefabrication workshops.
•
Operations & Reliability: Ensure the continuous availability of power and telecommunications services to prevent any disruption to off-site prefabrication activities or administrative operations.
2. Resource Management, Maintenance, and General Services
•
Temporary infrastructure maintenance: Plan and oversee routine and preventive maintenance for site infrastructure, manage facility modifications, oversee maintenance contractors, and ensure strict regulatory compliance for our facilities.
•
Resource availability: Continuously ensure the availability of the human, material, and technical resources required for the smooth daily operation of the site facilities and logistics areas.
•
Equipment and supply management: Handle the procurement, management, and maintenance of office furniture, IT and telephony equipment, screens, meeting projectors, general office supplies, and consumables.
•
Layout modifications and concurrent operations: Manage, adapt, and reorganize the layout of premises (offices, prefabrication areas, storage) based on construction phase progress, internal staffing changes, and the logistical constraints of our assembly subcontractors.
•
Hygiene and cleaning: Manage and supervise cleaning and waste management services for all our dedicated premises.
3. Client Shared Services Interface (SPOC)
•
Single Point of Contact: Act as the primary liaison with the end client regarding all matters related to site support services managed directly by them (e.g., site canteens, large communal changing rooms).
•
Data Consolidation: Gather requirements from our teams and relay our inputs (staffing forecasts, schedules, access requests) to the client to ensure our employees’ comfort and access to these shared facilities.
4. EHS, Security, Risk Management, and Continuous Improvement
•
Compliance with Site EHS Requirements: Ensure strict and absolute adherence to the safety, security, and environmental rules and standards mandated by the nuclear site operator across our entire site base (offices, storage, prefabrication areas).
•
Contribution to Risk Management: Identify administrative and logistical risks associated with the project. Actively participate in defining and implementing preventive and corrective measures in close collaboration with project teams.
•
Continuous Improvement: Identify areas for improvement within our installation and maintenance processes and drive concrete initiatives to boost operational efficiency while optimizing or reducing general service costs.
Candidate Profile
Education and Experience
•
Higher education qualification in General Services, Facility Management, Technical Building Management, or Civil/Electromechanical Engineering.
•
Extensive experience in a similar role, specifically gained on large-scale industrial construction sites (nuclear, petrochemical, or major infrastructure projects) involving the management of site facilities (base camps), complex temporary utility networks, and subcontractor coordination.
Required Skills:
•
Ability to size temporary installations, design site layout plans, and manage utility/energy network connections.
•
Proven experience in managing logistical interfaces and resolving conflicts arising from simultaneous work activities on the same site.
•
Knowledge of local network deployment (Wi-Fi, server racks) and management of collaborative equipment fleets (screens, projectors).
•
Ability to unite and align various stakeholders (internal teams, installation subcontractors, and the client) around shared layout and space-usage guidelines.
•
Strong ability to work independently to develop and maintain viable technical solutions based on client delivery points.
•
Strong internal customer focus to effectively meet the daily needs of production and project management teams.
•
Ability to communicate and negotiate skillfully with the end client (particularly regarding input for canteen/locker room facilities and the management of utility connection points).

• Experience in business capability and process taxonomies, maturity assessments and mapping gaps to enabling technology solutions.

At Dalcour Maclaren, we're key players in the Utilities and Infrastructure industry, bringing the UK and Ireland closer to Net Zero every day. Our land, environmental and geospatial experts work together to unlock the consents needed by our clients to deliver key projects. Our services include land access and assembly, agricultural liaison, planning, environmental impact assessments and geospatial mapping. Join us, and play your part in helping us to achieve our vision; to be the professional services team of choice, leading the Utilities and Infrastructure industry to a sustainable future.
What is our Graduate Surveyor programme?
The Graduate Surveying programme ensures our graduates achieve qualified status through either the MRICS (APC) or AssocRICS (ATC) pathways. Our training programme, coupled with extremely valuable ‘on the job’ experience, enables our graduates to realise their full potential as a working professional, in addition to achieving their ambitions to become the leading surveyors of the future.
What will you get up to? What does the job involve?
In a nutshell, our Graduate Surveyors will be working on utilities and infrastructure projects helping to manage land-related issues during the development of infrastructure like pipelines, power lines, or roads. Their role includes negotiating access agreements, assessing and handling compensation claims for landowners, ensuring compliance with regulations, and minimising the impact of projects on agricultural land and rural properties. You will act as the valuable intermediary between our clients and landowners, overseeing effective land access and management while ensuring fair compensation and resolving disputes.
A day in the life of a Graduate Surveyor could involve any of the following:
• Providing expertise: delivering land and property advice to a range of clients, helping them to make informed decisions.
• Heads of terms and licences: agreeing Heads of terms and contractual agreements with stakeholders on behalf of clients to aid the delivery of infrastructure projects
• Site noticing: getting out and about with your colleagues putting up notices to inform land owners of client schemes.
• Records of condition: reviewing and advising on various different land types, undertaking schedules of condition of private land
• Site visits: witnessing the tangible impact your work is having on Utilities & Infrastructure throughout the UK by seeing the projects in-person and monitoring their progress.
• Compensation and Valuation: assessing the financial impact of infrastructure projects, agreeing compensation claims; think valuation of land and property, agricultural losses, and general disturbance.
• Handling landlord and tenant relationships: overseeing tenancy agreements and ensuring legal compliance.
• Property and asset management: managing and optimising the performance of real estate and other tangible assets.
• Problem solving: working with the wider DM team and your clients to problem solve, advise on risks and reach solutions.
• Data and technology: delivering large scale schemes through innovative big data, technology and reporting functions
What do we need from you?
We don’t expect you to be an expert from day one, we're seeking the right combination of skills and attributes, like proactivity, problem-solving and a keen eye for detail that will contribute to your success.
However, to successfully enrol on our programme, you will need to hold a RICS accredited or relevant degree which will allow you to sit either your APC or ATC to become MRICS or AssocRICS qualified. Due to the nature of the role, a full UK driving licence and your own means of transport will also be essential.
Why join us?
In addition to a competitive salary, we also offer:
• A fully funded professional qualification (APC or ATC) with consistent support, mentoring and coaching from an experienced RICS training team plus our DM Academy, a team that is dedicated to your learning & development.
• Internal and external CPD events, interactive online training, offsite dedicated graduate training days.

Position
The Head of Treasury is responsible for leading Vesta's global treasury function, ensuring effective cash management, liquidity planning, banking operations, financial risk management, and treasury governance across a diverse portfolio of software businesses. Treasury & Cash Management

Banking & Financial Institutions

• Oversee treasury management systems, banking platforms, and payment technologies.
• Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, controls, and visibility of cash positions globally.
Strategic Finance Support
• Partner with Corporate Finance, M&A, and portfolio finance teams on acquisitions, integrations, and strategic projects.
• Provide treasury insight and analysis to senior leadership.
• Support capital allocation decisions and funding requirements across the business.

Leadership
• Build, develop, and mentor the treasury team.
• Establish best practice treasury processes across the organization in an international environment (Globally, specially Europe, Latam and the UK).
• Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
Qualifications, Skills & Experience
• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; professional qualification preferred.
• Extensive experience in treasury, corporate finance, banking, or financial management.
• Strong knowledge of cash management, liquidity planning, cash forecasting, treasury controls, debt facilities, and multi-currency environments.
• Excellent analytical, financial modelling, leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
• Experience within a global, multi-entity organisation is highly desirable.
• High level of integrity, professionalism, and attention to detail.
Personal Characteristics
• Strategic thinker with a hands-on approach.
• Highly organised, commercially minded, and results focused.
• Strong relationship builder and collaborator.
• Naturally inquisitive with a continuous improvement mindset.

POLITICO is seeking a highly capable and dynamic Senior Booking Producer to join our growing Live team in Europe. POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital.

Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy. Job Description
A front-row seat to the science of work
When it comes to shaping how one of the UK’s largest organisations works, traditional HR can only take us so far. We need data that leaves no room for guesswork. Technology that keeps people and processes connected. And strategy that’s born out of insight. Exactly what our People & Places teams do every single day.
But they don’t do it alone. Our occupational psychologists are the people behind the people – using behavioural science, research and insight to understand what makes work work better. Join us on the Occupational Psychology Graduate Scheme and see how it all happens up close.
2 years. Three rotations.
You’ll do the hard yards in a training-to-profession scheme that puts you front and centre of occupational psychology in action. And along the way, you’ll:
•
Bring your scientific know-how, insight and creativity to the most important challenges we face as an organisation
•
Understand how psychology is used in a real business setting
•
Help improve performance and wellbeing by improving how we work and make decisions
The work you could be doing
Throughout the scheme, you’ll find yourself touching a range of projects within the People function. Whether it’s assessment and selection or performance and development, you’ll back every decision you make with data and research. You’ll also:
•
Decode how collaboration, office design and colleague experience can drive engagement, productivity and wellbeing
•
Conduct applied research and lead projects to uncover what drives performance
•
Evaluate our existing people systems and frameworks and understand how we can improve performance management, leadership capability and talent processes
•
Analyse colleague data to explain patterns, challenge assumptions and influence how the organisation functions
•
Create frameworks and guidance that make way for occupational psychology to be used throughout the business
•
Design fair and effective assessments that improve how we evaluate potential, performance and development
And whatever you do, you won’t be doing it alone. A dedicated supervisor will always have your back, so you’ll stay on track with your own development as well. You’ll also have access to a growing community of Occupational Psychologists across the Group, giving you plenty of opportunities to learn and make your mark as part of a function that’s always evolving.
What you’ll take away
By the end of the scheme, you’ll have the skills, the confidence and the experience to apply psychology in a commercial environment – where everything you do will improve how we work together to serve our customers. You’ll also complete a fully funded Stage 2 training, working towards Chartered Psychologist status.
Requirements
What you need to apply
•
Be eligible for the Graduate Basis for Chartered Membership
•
Be currently studying towards or have completed a BPS-accredited Master’s in Occupational Psychology
•
While we do not require a set projected minimum degree achievement, we strongly recommend the ability to be able to demonstrate sound knowledge, understanding and technical skills aligned to the role. Some aspects of this, alongside behaviours and values, will be assessed through the application process.

We cannot sponsor visas.
Location

Job Description:
The opportunity
Leonardo offers a range of Apprenticeships from 2-5yrs. across a variety of STEM and business routes, offering paid training, coupled with on the job learning that enables you to gain practical skills, experience and knowledge that sets up the best start to your career. We offer competitive entry salaries and fully support your academic learning through to qualifications, with salary increases as you progress.
We support helping you settle into your new location ensuring you are familiar with the team and have a warm welcome from day 1. There is a member of our Apprentice team at each site, helping you progress, ensuring your study time is protected, enabling access to digital learning as well as opportunities to get involved with the local community and STEM projects, enhance many aspects of each programme.
What you will do as a Project Controls Apprentice,
You will help our project teams plan, monitor and successfully deliver complex projects and bids. Working alongside experienced professionals and benefitting from placements within different areas of the business, you’ll develop skills in project planning, scheduling, cost management, risk management and performance reporting.
You’ll learn how to use data and project controls tools to understand progress, identify potential issues and help teams make informed decisions to drive project success. You’ll work with people from across the business, building your network and gaining hands-on experience while working towards a recognised qualification thereby building the foundations for a successful career in Project Controls.
The Leonardo Project Controls Apprenticeship is structured around a programme of placements that will see you move around the business within the Project Controls Function over a 3.5 year period and is designed to give you as much experience and exposure to Project Controls practices and different operational contexts as possible. This will help you develop strong core skills of Project Controls whilst also giving you a wider understanding of how a global business operates.
You will also undertake a Level 3 Project Controls Technician qualification over this time to compliment on the job learning alongside internal training to understand and utilise globally recognised tool sets and standards in Project Controls.
The role requires:
You don’t need previous experience in Project Controls. We’re looking for people who are curious, motivated to learn and keen to build a career working on exciting and complex projects.
You could be a great fit if you:
• Enjoy working with numbers and information, and are interested in understanding what the data is telling you.
• Are organised and methodical, with an eye for detail and the ability to manage different tasks and priorities.
• Have a curious mindset and enjoy asking questions, solving problems and finding better ways of doing things.
• Are a good communicator who is comfortable working with others and building positive relationships.
• Enjoy being part of a team and are willing to contribute your ideas and listen to different perspectives.
• Are comfortable using digital tools and technology, and keen to develop your skills further.
• Are proactive and willing to take responsibility, asking for help when you need it and learning from feedback.
• Have a genuine enthusiasm to learn and develop, both through your apprenticeship studies and through hands-on experience in the workplace.
Qualifications:
You must have (as a minimum) the following qualifications:
5 GCSE grades 4 - 9 or grades A*- C or equivalent, to include Maths and English
The starting salary for this role is £20,000
During your Apprenticeship we require you to spend at least 3/4 days a week on site to integrate with your team, connect socially and maximise your learning experience.
Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting

At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do, key contributors in shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive.

• Rewarding performance: All employees are eligible for our bonus scheme.

• Tailored perks: Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more.

We’ll reward you with a starting salary of £29,400 pro rata.

• Experience first-hand what it’s like working in a purpose-driven organisation

Forward Deployed Engineers take AI solutions from idea to secure production inside live client environments. Job Description
Your Role: Digital Infrastructure Engineer
Join the Outdoor Digital Infrastructure team and help keep the technology behind Global’s digital advertising estate reliable, resilient and ready to evolve. Reporting to the Head of Outdoor Digital Service Management, you will support infrastructure across the UK and Ireland, including London’s TfL travel network.
As a Digital Infrastructure Engineer at Global, you will:
Key Responsibilities
• Develop digital infrastructure: Document existing capabilities and business requirements, then implement new and improved digital infrastructure in line with agreed designs, standards and protocols.
• Resolve incidents and problems: Take ownership of third-line incidents through to resolution, coordinating with external suppliers where needed. Identify recurring issues, establish root causes and workarounds, and deliver or support permanent fixes.
• Manage change and deployment: Raise, plan, implement and review changes in line with agreed processes. Work closely with project, technology and on-site installation teams to deliver safe, reliable end-to-end deployments.
• Support operational teams: Provide technical expertise to first-line teams, particularly during live incidents and deployments, and maintain clear, useful documentation that supports effective service delivery.
• Deliver out-of-hours works: Take technical responsibility for planned installations and operational activities, including regular overnight work, ensuring delivery is safe, correct and to the required standard.
What You’ll Love About This Role
• Think Big: Help shape the digital infrastructure behind Outdoor advertising across the UK and Ireland.
• Own It: Take responsibility for technical delivery, service improvements and resolving issues that matter.
• Keep it Simple: Turn defined designs and processes into practical, dependable solutions.
• Better Together: Partner with project teams, suppliers, installers and colleagues across Global to deliver great outcomes.
What Success Looks Like
In your first few months, you’ll have:
• Built a strong understanding of Global’s core Outdoor digital infrastructure and key documentation.
• Achieved the required Sentinel certification for safe working on the railway.
• Become confident using core applications, including the relevant content management system.
• Developed an understanding of IP schemas, connectivity relationships and project requirements.
• Contributed improvements to team documentation and resolved common incident types independently.
What You’ll Need
• Infrastructure experience: Experience supporting Windows desktop and server environments, Linux operating systems and core infrastructure technologies such as DNS, DHCP, HTTP(S), IIS or Apache.
• Network and remote support skills: Confidence using remote management tools, networking technologies and scripting tools such as PowerShell to diagnose and resolve issues.
• Technical delivery: Experience implementing technical solutions, integrating off-the-shelf products and supporting small to medium-sized technical projects.
• Service management: Experience working with an IT service management tool and within an ITIL-aligned environment, including incident, problem and change management.
• Digital platform knowledge: Experience supporting digital advertising, digital signage or a comparable content management platform in a live environment.
• Collaborative approach: Able to work effectively with technical and non-technical colleagues, suppliers and customer-facing teams, prioritising work according to impact and risk.
• Continuous learning: Proactive about developing technical, industry-specific and safety knowledge. ITIL Foundation, relevant Microsoft certifications and a Level 3 IT qualification or equivalent are beneficial.
